description: This pie chart displays the error distribution in Audio-Reasoner, divided into seven distinct categories. The slices are arranged sequentially by size, ordered in an ascending manner clockwise starting from the top vertical axis. The smallest slice, colored pale turquoise, represents "Wrong Understanding of Instruction" at 3%, followed by a pale cyan slice for "Choice Format Error" at 4%, and a sky blue slice for "Lack of Knowledge" at 9%. Continuing clockwise, the next slice is light blue and labeled "Repeat Thinking and No Answer" at 12%, followed by a periwinkle slice representing "Correct Answer but Wrong Choice" at 15%. A lavender slice denotes "Reasoning Error" at 20%, and finally, the largest slice, colored light purple, accounts for "Perceptual Error" at 37%. The chart does not include a separate legend; instead, the four largest segments contain their text labels and percentages directly inside the slices, while the three smallest segments have their text labels and percentages positioned outside the chart with thin black arrows pointing to their respective slices. All segments are separated by thin white border lines, and no individual slices are exploded, offset, or otherwise visually emphasized.
